problem.text: Let $(a, b, c)$ be the real number solution of the system of equations $x^3 - xyz = 2$, $y^3 - xyz = 6$, $z^3 - xyz = 20$. The greatest possible value of $a^3 + b^3 + c^3$ can be written in the form $\frac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers. Find $m + n$.

steps.title: Where to start: every equation shares the term $xyz$
steps.body: A solution $(a, b, c)$ satisfies $a^3 - abc = 2$, $b^3 - abc = 6$ and $c^3 - abc = 20$. The same product $abc$ appears in all three, so call it $p = abc$. Then $a^3 = 2 + p$, $b^3 = 6 + p$ and $c^3 = 20 + p$: everything depends on the single number $p$.

your_turn.prompt: Add the three equations $a^3 = 2 + p$, $b^3 = 6 + p$, $c^3 = 20 + p$. What is $a^3 + b^3 + c^3$ in terms of $p$?

steps.title: Find an equation for $p$
steps.body: So we need the possible values of $p$. Multiplying the three equations gives $a^3b^3c^3 = (2+p)(6+p)(20+p)$, and the left side is $(abc)^3 = p^3$. $$p^3 = (2+p)(6+p)(20+p)$$

steps.title: Solve the quadratic
steps.body: The $p^3$ terms cancel, leaving $28p^2 + 172p + 240 = 0$. Dividing by $4$ gives $7p^2 + 43p + 60 = 0$, which factors as $(7p + 15)(p + 4) = 0$. So $p = -\frac{15}{7}$ or $p = -4$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Both values of $p$ really occur: take the real cube roots $a = \sqrt[3]{2+p}$, $b = \sqrt[3]{6+p}$, $c = \sqrt[3]{20+p}$; then $(abc)^3 = p^3$, and since real cube roots are unique, $abc = p$. Now $28 + 3(-4) = 16$ and $28 + 3\left(-\frac{15}{7}\right) = \frac{151}{7} \approx 21.6$, so the greatest value is $\frac{151}{7}$, already in lowest terms because $151$ is prime. Then $m + n = 151 + 7 = 158$. The answer is **$158$**.
